title: chore(client): declare and assert the Node engine floor across every client build path
intent: PR #279 raises @vitejs/plugin-vue to 6.0.8, whose declared engine is ^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0 (up from ^18.0.0 || >=20.0.0). The repo had no machine-readable Node floor anywhere: packages/client/package.json had no engines field, and there is no .nvmrc, .node-version, or .npmrc. Every client build path resolved Node from a bare major (setup-node 20, ARG NODE_VERSION=20), which satisfies the new floor today only because floating tags resolve upward. This patch declares the floor once and asserts it at every build entry point, so a downward change or a stale cached base image fails with a named error instead of an opaque Vite/ESM failure. It does not change the resolved Node version on any current build path.

diff_articulation.what_changed: packages/client/package.json gains engines.node = '^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0', the single declared source of truth, mirroring @vitejs/plugin-vue 6.x. packages/client/.nvmrc (new) pins 20.19.0 for local shells. The four client Dockerfiles (docker/client/Dockerfile, .production, .railway, and packages/client/Dockerfile - the last of which is live via packages/client/railway.json dockerfilePath) each gain one RUN node -e assertion immediately after the builder FROM, exiting 1 with a named message when the base image is below the floor. client_lint_build.yml changes node-version from the bare major 20 to the range '^20.19.0' - still resolving the newest 20.x so security patches land, but now failing at setup-node rather than mid-build if the floor is ever unmet. containers.yml, docker-compose.yml, docker-compose.production.yml and .env.example keep NODE_VERSION=20 (which floats above the floor) and gain comments naming the floor and its source; docker-compose.yml's stale '20+ required for Vite 5' comment is corrected.
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: No existing mechanism encodes a Node floor for this workspace - no engines field, no .nvmrc, no .npmrc, no CI assertion - so nothing today would catch a regression to Node 18 or 20.9 except an opaque downstream build failure. The Dockerfile assertion is not redundant with the workflow change: four of the five client-image call sites (core_ci.yml:181, proxy_parity.yml:44, proxy_adaptive.yml:43, publish-images.yml:159) pass no NODE_VERSION build-arg at all and silently inherit the Dockerfile ARG default, so a workflow-only fix would leave them uncovered.

commands_run: sh -c with the RUN payload extracted verbatim from docker/client/Dockerfile -> exit 0 on Node 24.11.0; confirms the quoting survives Dockerfile RUN shell form
npm ci --dry-run --no-audit --no-fund in packages/client -> added 459 packages, exit 0, no EBADENGINE
yaml.safe_load over client_lint_build.yml, containers.yml, docker-compose.yml, docker-compose.production.yml -> all OK
assertion that no build-args block-scalar line starts with '#' or lacks '=' -> PASS (an earlier draft leaked a comment into containers.yml build-args; corrected before commit)
docker build NOT run - the local Docker daemon is not running; the Dockerfile assertion is verified by executing its exact payload through sh -c, not by an image build

architecture_scan.acknowledgement_notes: Build-time guard only; no application code, no runtime behavior, and no resolved-version change on any current build path. The single non-comment functional edit outside the guards is client_lint_build.yml node-version 20 -> ^20.19.0, which resolves to the same Node release today. Deliberately NOT done: hard-pinning NODE_VERSION to the literal floor 20.19.0, which would have moved every image from the newest 20.x down to an older patch level and dropped security fixes for no safety gain.
